importRaw.N2: BACKGROUND: Although hamstring strain injuries (HSI) are commonly reported injuries in football, there are limited studies on the incidence of HSI and its intrinsic factors in Malaysian football settings. The aim of this study was to examine the incidence of HSI among Malaysian footballers and study intrinsic risk factors (hamstring strength, intra and interlimb deficits) associated with the risk of HSI. METHOD(S): This is a cohort study of 81 Malaysian professional footballers in a single renowned club. This study was conducted throughout 2023 Malaysian Football League. Preseason medical assessments include demographic data, anthropometric assessments, and isometric hamstring and quadriceps strength. Injury surveillance was done throughout the season. RESULT(S): The incidence of HSI was 0.91 injuries per 1000 H, with the incidence of injury during match was higher 5.43 injuries per 1000 H compared to training 0.42 injuries per 1000 H. Weight (Odds Ratio [OR]: 7.83, CI: 0.36-1.4, P=0.07), previous history of hamstring injury (OR: 10.3, CI: 0.41-259, P=0.156), hamstring deficit >15% (OR: 119.1, CI: 0.54-34.79, P=0.06), and hamstring: quadriceps ratio (OR: 43.23, CI: 0.48-38.79, P=0.10), were identified as predictors of risk of future HSI. CONCLUSION(S): Hamstring deficit and low H:Q ratio were the modifiable risk factors of HSI and should be considered in a hamstring injury prevention program.Copyright © 2024 EDIZIONI MINERVA MEDICA.
